headline: Record first-half profit as production hits new highs
summary_short: PetroChina's H1 2026 net profit attributable to shareholders rose 22% y/y to RMB103.94B — crossing RMB100B in a half-year for the first time — on revenue of RMB1,527.49B (+5.3% y/y); Q2-standalone EPS of ¥0.31 rose 17.4% q/q.
summary_long: H1 2026 net profit attributable to shareholders climbed 22% y/y to RMB103.94B on revenue up 5.3% y/y to RMB1,527.49B, with basic EPS of RMB0.57. Oil-and-gas-equivalent output reached 921 million barrels (domestic crude 393 million barrels, marketable natural gas 2.66 trillion cubic feet), both record first-half levels. Segment operating profit: oil, gas and new energies RMB100.45B; natural gas marketing RMB24.09B; refining, chemicals and new materials RMB14.53B; marketing RMB11.36B. The board declared an interim dividend of RMB0.26 per share, record date 15 September 2026. Q2-standalone EPS of ¥0.31 rose 17.4% q/q from ¥0.264.
confidence_notes: PetroChina's SEC registration (CIK 0001108329) has no filings since Feb 2024 (ADR deregistered) — the EDGAR CIK-list fetch (Rung 3) returned nothing covering FY2026, so filing depth is sourced from the company's PRNewswire-hosted H1 2026 results release (a sanctioned wire host, not an aggregator) rather than a 10-Q/20-F/6-K. H1 cumulative figures (net profit, revenue, EPS RMB0.57) are not on the same basis as the shard's Q2-standalone EPS (¥0.31, Yahoo earningsChart) — both are reported here but not diffed against each other. The release did not disclose capex, buybacks, or quantified price/volume attribution for the profit move.

drivers.explanation: Not explained in the release beyond record production and general commentary on responding to oil-market volatility; no quantified price/volume attribution was given.
